rounds.question: Where does the chat live, and how does it show what it did?

variants.name: Current popover
variants.idea: The Write page popover: one prompt, one generation, no thread, no tools beyond writing the page.
variants.cost: No follow-ups, no library, stats or publishing from the prompt

variants.name: Side panel
variants.idea: A steady conversation beside the draft, with changes connected to the canvas.
variants.cost: A narrower page canvas and a scrolling thread.

variants.name: Chat and preview
variants.axis: Chat-first split: the conversation on the left, the page on the right as its output
variants.idea: Opening the chat turns the editor into two columns. Each turn that changed the page ends in a numbered draft revision card, and matching numbered markers on the page point back to that turn.
variants.cost: While the chat is open the editor header becomes a thin preview toolbar and the page narrows by 420 px; Style and Share wait in the full editor

variants.name: Grown popover
variants.idea: The familiar Write page popover grows into a thread, with live work carried by its header button when closed.
variants.cost: A compact thread needs scrolling, and the page moves left while chat is open.

variants.name: Bottom dock
variants.idea: A page-width composer with a thread that opens upward and folds away to reveal changes.
variants.cost: Long conversations compete with the lower canvas.

variants.name: At the block
variants.idea: Select a block to ask about it; review numbered changes and undo at the block.
variants.cost: Context switches between the page and a narrow thread.

variants.name: One assistant everywhere
variants.idea: Ask Clarity is a sidebar entry and Cmd+J that opens one resizable right panel in the app shell. The same thread follows the rep from Home into the editor, scoped by a removable context chip, and answers come back as leads, pages and a publish card the rep acts on in place.
variants.cost: A new app-wide panel and nav entry rather than a popover; needs one thread persisted across routes
variants.why: The chat can do everything the MCP can, so it belongs to the app, not the editor; a right panel is the convention reps already know.

variants.name: Command bar
variants.idea: A keyboard-first command bar holds quick follow-ups, then tucks into a result pill to return the page to view.
variants.cost: Long conversations need scrolling and temporarily obscure the page.
